note: v4 trial workers (Phase 3A, 2026-11-08, Nusrat; declared before the first Phase 3A session). Read by TrialRunnerV4 in WarehouseRobot_v4.unity only; nothing in the v3 scene reads it. Every value is scenario design (who stands where, what the commander shows); no Python threshold is set or changed here.
data_splits_note: Anisha's file, read only. Each run's looks and clips must lie wholly in the session mode's split (Python's data_splits_v4.guard_run, repeated in Unity: DataSplitsV4.GuardRun); a development session refuses the test look and the test clips before anything is recorded.
forward_command_note: 2026-11-12 (Avatar/Config/upgrade_design.md section 2, declared before it was built): when goal B's branch is the node's FORWARD branch (always at the start node A) the commander shows PROCEED (the forearm swing) instead of a POINT; every other branch is a POINT (option A stance kept).
scenario_note: direction: the commander answers every ask with the direction (PROCEED or POINT). Declared development scenarios (upgrade_design.md section 6), selected per session with a copy in Avatar/Config/sessions/ (TrialPlayV4 -workersConfig): wait_then_direction (at every ask first WAIT, then the direction within the same ask, inside Python's 20 s WAIT timeout) and stop_while_driving (once per run, while the robot drives toward the node where the commander stands and is distance_m from it, the commander shows STOP for hold_s, then lowers it; the robot must stop and resume).
commander_note: The commander answers every 'Which direction?' (worker_v4.json question.prompt; a new ask also when the text changes to ' (asking again)') with a POINT along the branch toward goal B: the world direction from the junction to the branch's next node (Python's branch yaw, hri_control_v4.branch_directions). The gesture starts only after the question is shown (WorkerV4 scheduler); a gesture not yet started is dropped when the question disappears. WAIT-then-POINT and STOP scripts are Phase 3B.
looks_note: Empty = every look of the session mode's split in data_splits.json, in name order. Run r: commander looks[(r - 1) mod n], bystander k looks[(r - 1 + k) mod n]. Each worker keeps its look for the whole run (the workers are spawned per run).
layout_note: ONE commander, moved to the stand of the junction the robot is sent to (the moved-worker layout of both reported v3 Task 2 results, AUDIT.md section 12), and moved only once it is idle. Not one standing worker per junction: truth.jsonl lists every worker in the scene, and Python's evaluation calls a run a bystander run when truth.jsonl has more than one worker_id (hri_eval_dev_v4.Run.bystanders), so standing workers would mark every run as a bystander run.

bystanders.note: count: extra workers (worker_id 2, 3, ...) at the first count stands, in the same frame as the roadmap's worker stand (ahead_m along the arrival direction at the junction, right_m to its right): J1 ahead-left, moved ahead to 4.0 m, and J2 ahead-left, moved left to 4.5 m (the corner opposite the commander's stand; 2026-11-12 upgrade_design.md section 13: the J1 behind-right stand of the first R3 session is removed and both ahead-left stands moved out). They notice and face the robot like the commander but never gesture, so they never gesture after the question (CLAUDE.local.md: no distractor gestures unless declared with Anisha). is_commander is false for them. Each stand is refused unless it is at least min_road_clearance_m from every roadmap road (the robot never drives into a bystander), at least min_commander_distance_m from every commander stand (the robot's ask positions are about 2 m from the commander), on a free cell of the ground-truth grid and not inside a collider. Since 2026-11-12 each stand must also be at least nearer_margin_m farther from the robot than the commander's stand at every point of the robot's approach to every ask node: the last approach_m of the arrival road up to the node (= drive.junction_slow_radius_m of robot_vision/configs/hri_control.json; at the start node, the start position), so the robot, which approaches the nearest person it sees when it scans, never chooses a bystander. 0 = no bystanders.

max_active_avatars_note: A session is refused when 1 commander + bystanders.count is above this, or when more WorkerV4 avatars are active in the scene. 4 was set for three bystander stands plus the commander and is kept (two stands since 2026-11-12, upgrade_design.md section 13); frame times are logged in every telemetry message (frame_ms_list, frame_ms_max) so the cost of each extra avatar is measured in the development sessions.
